messages:
tess: Heads-up — staged rollout for release 0.3.7 is showing a p95 latency spike on next-gen nodes. p95 ~ 2.8s (baseline ~0.9s), p50 up ~1.5x. KV miss rate jumped during canary traffic. We’re at 10% rollout.

deploy-bot: [ci/perf-check] release/0.3.7 failed perf-check on canary — see https://ci.redwood/12345 (automated alert).

ops-bot: autoslo: p95_latency > 2s for 5m -> staged rollout PAUSED at 12% (autoslo trigger).

joel: can you paste the root logs + commit that went in last night?

tess: commit 5ac8f2d (https://git.redwood/commit/5ac8f2d). quick tail of canary logs:
```
[2026-03-17T22:03:11Z] ROUTE=embedder-canary p50=420ms p95=2810ms KV_MISS_RATE=0.21->0.89 KV_EVICTIONS=4800/min
[2026-03-17T22:03:12Z] kernel=fused_attention_v2 selected for shard-3
[2026-03-17T22:03:12Z] batch_size=16 prefetch_window=32
```

maya: sounds like a candidate set: kernel selector change (prefers fused kernel on A100s) + adaptive prefetch/dynamic batching tweaks. Both PRs merged last night. I can run a bisect plan. Thought: start with kernel selector revert as it's narrow.

rachel: uploaded a quick 30s flamegraph from the canary pod: https://artifacts.redwood/flame/1976543210.svg — main hotspots: KVLookup::handle_miss, and fused_attention_v2::prefetch_read. Looks correlated with prefetch window growth and higher KV miss churn.

joel: which PR changed kernel_autoselect default? I recall #8241 from liam touched that.

liam: yep, PR #8241 toggled kernel_autoselect to prefer fused for 'a100-xlarge' by default. PR #8300 enabled adaptive prefetch for dynamic_batching. Both in same deploy.

maya: bisect plan:
```
# quick bisect outline (canary nodes)
git checkout release/0.3.7
# try reverting kernel_autoselect first
git revert --no-commit 5ac8f2d
# build + deploy to a single canary shard (route: embedder-canary/shard-3)
./deploy/canary.sh --shards=1 --config=patch-revert-kernel.yaml
monitor metrics (p95, kv_miss, kv_evictions) for 15m
```

rachel: lower-risk mitigation: reduce prefetch_window for canary from 32 -> 8 via runtime config patch. That should reduce KV pressure fast while we bisect. Example patch: 
```
runtime:
  dynamic_batching:
    prefetch_window: 8
    enabled: true
```
Apply as a config override to the canary group.

ops-bot: applied rollout PAUSE and pinned canary traffic to previous model variant snapshot (snap-20260316). Auto-notify on resume.

deploy-bot: opened revert candidate PR: https://git.redwood/pull/19765 (revert: kernel_autoselect preference). Title: "revert: prefer-fused-default on a100" by joel.

tess: I’ll apply rachel's prefetch_window patch to the canary patch channel now to buy time. If metrics improve, we can continue with a narrower revert. If not, prioritize revert PR.

joel: ack — starting a monitored deploy of the prefetch patch to shard-3. I’ll watch KV_EVICTIONS and p95 for 15m. If p95 drops to <1.2x baseline and KV_MISS_RATE < 0.3, we keep the patch and run bisect on kernel selector vs batching.

maya: attaching bisect checklist: 1) isolate kernel revert, 2) test prefetch-only revert, 3) if neither, run binary search between the two PRs, 4) collect flamegraphs at each step, 5) collect KV TTL/eviction histograms.

rachel: FYI eviction histogram before patch: 95th eviction latency ~ 180ms, after deploy peaked at ~480ms. Also seeing increased KV writeback pressure.

liam: sorry team — I’ll stand by to revert #8241 if metrics don't recover. I already added a quick opt-out flag: `kernel_autoselect.enabled=false` can be rolled via runtime config.

ops-bot: note: autoslo rule doc for staged rollouts: p95 > 2x baseline for >= 5m -> pause + alert + optional auto-revert if p95 > 2.5x for >= 10m. Current p95 peaked at ~3.1x for 6m.

tess: decision: pause rollout (done), apply prefetch_window=8 to canary (in progress), prepare kernel_autoselect revert PR as hot option, run bisect if needed. Owners: joel (revert PR + monitor), maya (bisect), rachel (profiling + flamegraphs).

joel: will merge revert PR if metrics don't recover within 20m post-patch. pinging @liam for immediate rollback permission.

liam: granted — go ahead if we don't see recovery.

rachel: small suggestion for future guardrails: add KV eviction rate as a gating metric for kernel selector changes (threshold: eviction_rate_increase > 2x baseline).

maya: +1 — also propose a short CI perf smoke for merges that touch both kernel selection and batching heuristics.

tess: thanks all. I’ll post an incident note if we end up reverting. Otherwise will close this thread when rollout resumes. :white_check_mark:

joel: quick status update: 10m after prefetch patch — p95 down to 1.05x baseline, KV_MISS_RATE -> 0.28, evictions trending down. Holding for 10 more minutes.

rachel: confirmed flamegraph shows reduced time in prefetch path after patch.

liam: great — standby keeping revert PR open but unmerged.

ops-bot: autoslo: resume conditions met? p95 stable below 2x for 12m -> leaving rollout paused manual resume only.

maya: ack. will continue bisect in background but deprioritize until next deploy window.

joel: final: will close revert PR if stable for 1h, leaving runtime config patch as temporary mitigation and open a follow-up to tune kernel_autoselect heuristics.

rachel: noted — creating follow-up ticket: RED-ENG-4387 (kernel selector + KV guardrails).

liam: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
